_comment: Footsteps, as recordings rather than recipes. Everything else this game makes a noise with is
synthesised from Data/sounds.json, and a footstep is where that stops being good enough: it is a
physical event with a texture, and texture is the one thing a handful of tunable numbers cannot
Each surface names its clips, kept in a folder of their own named for it. One is picked at random
per footfall and its pitch is nudged, so a run down a corridor does not turn into a metronome.
Every clip is mono 48 kHz, its lead-in silence cut, capped at 0.6 s with a short fade, and brought to
the same loudness (RMS about -23.7 dB, as concrete). gain is then how loud a step on that surface is
against the others, by ear: soft ground quieter than hard floor. Metal is boots on aluminium; dirt a
soft step with sand grit mixed in; mud a step with a squelch, and wet steps.
